parsed.explanation: Traveller-facing exposures are limited. Gender identity is protected under federal sex-discrimination law, and a 2024 national ruling awarded damages for exclusion from a service, showing a remedy operating for visitors. Nothing documents a birth-sex facility rule for visitors, border or document friction, or an enforced presentation offence. Same-sex conduct is decriminalised. Remaining exposures are: (1) a 2023 custody standard in one state/province that defaults to lived gender but leaves staff discretion and excludes post-surgical trans prisoners, documented from a single source; (2) national research describing systemic discrimination and organised exclusionary campaigns, though not quantified for visitor settings and partly dated; (3) a 2003 brief on public assault and harassment, which is dated; (4) a current under-18 care restriction that does not reach adult visitors. Hate-crime provisions have no prosecution data, so they count as only partial recourse. Acceptance is documented (pride events, a court protecting a trans woman from an activist) but uneven across jurisdictions. Overall this sits in the reduced-risk band, below the acceptance-plus-protection tier because of the single-state custody gap and the unquantified discrimination record.
